**Why**

- **How to settle it:** if multi-line invoices still drift after this fix, look up one invoice in Ledgerline where the methods differ. # Fix: invoice totals one cent off from Ledgerline

All 4 tests pass (`python3 -m pytest -q`), including `test_inv_2291` (total 1.38). The same text is in `NOTES.md`. One question stays open and needs finance: whether Ledgerline computes VAT per line or once on the subtotal.

## What changed
- `invoicing/totals.py`: added `to_cent()`, which rounds to the cent with an explicit `ROUND_HALF_UP`. It now handles both roundings (line net and VAT). Both used to call `quantize(CENT)` with no mode, which falls back to Python's decimal default, `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.
- `tests/test_totals.py`: added `test_line_net_rounds_half_up`, using exact-half line nets 0.225 and 0.125, so the line-net change is guarded too. I checked that this test and `test_inv_2291` both fail on the old rounding and pass on the new.

## Why
INV-2291 has a subtotal of 1.25 at 10%, so VAT is exactly 0.125. Half-even rounds that to 0.12 (total 1.37). Ledgerline rounds half-up to 0.13 (total 1.38). The same one-cent gap appears whenever an amount lands on an exact half-cent after an even digit. `docs/accounting-rules.md` rule 2 already says Ledgerline rounds half-up, and the code didn't follow it. `line_net` had the same fault, so I fixed it there too. No reported Ledgerline example covers the line-net case; that change follows rule 2.

## Open question, not changed: VAT per line or once on the subtotal?
The findings mirror returned one relevant entry (`6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412`, 2026-09-14, author unknown). It agrees on half-up, and I confirmed that part. It also claims Ledgerline computes VAT per line (round each line's VAT half-up, then sum) instead of once on the subtotal. I did not adopt that claim:
- It is a single uncorroborated note from an unknown author. The other mirror entry is an unrelated pytest note. The note's evidence (an export of about 200 invoices) isn't available here, and it may describe a different Ledgerline setup.
- Nothing in this repo can tell the two methods apart. INV-2291 and the other tests give identical totals both ways.
- The two methods disagree on about a third of random invoices (1-6 lines, 5-21% VAT), so a wrong guess would cause new one-cent mismatches.

The code keeps its existing behavior (VAT once on the subtotal), with a short comment pointing to this question. To settle it, ask finance for Ledgerline's total on a multi-line invoice where the methods differ. Example: two lines of 0.05 at 10%. VAT on the subtotal gives a total of 0.11, per-line gives 0.12. If Ledgerline shows 0.12, VAT in `invoice_totals` needs to be rounded per line and summed. The note doesn't say whether each line's VAT comes from the rounded or the unrounded line net, so check an invoice with fractional quantities as well. Add whichever invoice finance confirms as a test.

## Summary: invoice totals one cent off from Ledgerline (fixed)

The totals now match Ledgerline for INV-2291 (1.38). `python3 -m pytest -q` gives 5 passed; it was 1 failed and 2 passed before. I checked against `docs/accounting-rules.md` and the single Ledgerline figure in the report. I have no access to Ledgerline itself. The same text is in `NOTES.md` at the project root.

**Cause.** Both `quantize(CENT)` calls in `invoicing/totals.py` had no rounding mode. Decimal then used its default, half-even (banker's rounding), but `docs/accounting-rules.md` says Ledgerline uses half-up. The two only differ on exact ties, which is why the mismatch is only "sometimes". For INV-2291 the VAT is 1.25 x 0.10 = 0.125. We rounded it to 0.12 (total 1.37). Half-up gives 0.13 (total 1.38).

**Change.**
- `invoicing/totals.py`:
  - A new `to_cent()` rounds with an explicit `ROUND_HALF_UP`.
  - It is used for both the VAT and `line_net`, which had the same bug but isn't covered by the reported test.
  - The result no longer depends on the ambient decimal context. I confirmed INV-2291 still gives 1.38 under a `ROUND_DOWN` context.
- `tests/test_totals.py`: I added two tests.
  - `test_line_net_rounds_half_up` covers the line-net path.
  - `test_rounding_is_half_up_not_always_up` guards against over-correcting to "always round up".
  - With the old half-even rounding swapped back in at runtime, `test_inv_2291` and `test_line_net_rounds_half_up` fail, so they do catch the bug.

**Open questions I did not change.**
- **Per-line VAT:** VAT is still computed once on the invoice subtotal, as before.
  - INV-2291 can't tell that apart from VAT computed per line (both give 0.13), and the docs don't say which Ledgerline does.
  - They differ on other invoices. Two 0.04 lines at 10% give 0.01 on the subtotal and 0.00 per line.
  - If finance still sees one-cent differences after this fix, compare a multi-line invoice against Ledgerline next.
- **Negative amounts (credit notes):** half-up breaks ties away from zero (-0.125 becomes -0.13). The docs don't say how Ledgerline treats negative ties, and nothing tests it.

Both returned 0 hits, so nothing from it was used. The queries are logged in `.findings/queries.log`, which the tool wrote. Nothing was published anywhere. I ran no git or bd commands.

**Housekeeping.** I created no scratch files, so there is no `tmp/` folder. I removed the `__pycache__` and `.pytest_cache` directories my test runs had generated.
